limits: No false path is added for the synchronous reset.
I/O delays are 20 percent of the original GUI clock period; drive/load and further physical defaults are retained in the resolved tool configuration.
Routing DRC and extracted STA may run before the cutoff; signoff DRC/LVS and SDF simulation are separate stages.
The existing finite generic netlist test is a prerequisite, not verification of the newly technology-mapped netlist.

This profile reuses original technology mapping and pre-CTS placement, builds a new clock tree with cluster size 8 to leave headroom for clock dummy loads under the unchanged fanout limit 10, then runs standard post-GRT repair and fresh detailed routing/extraction/stream-out. No timing or electrical constraint is relaxed. A changed layout requires new DRC/LVS and post-route functional validation.

The v2 actual clock tree retained four internal clock trunks with 16 loads against the unchanged fanout limit 10. Version 3 adds the standard CTS buffer spacing of 50 micrometres; success is determined by the actual new reports, never inferred from this parameter.

Version 4 explicitly optimizes and checks intermediate routing at max_ss_100C_1v60 with 30 percent slew/capacitance repair margins. A separate PnR-only SDC uses fanout 8 to reserve antenna-diode headroom. Final signoff retains the original SDC, fanout 10, 0.75 ns slew, original cell capacitance limits and all nine STA corners. Intermediate estimates never establish extracted closure.
